ch03.c.goal.proj: Components are projections onto the axes: $A_x = A\cos\theta$, $A_y = A\sin\theta$
ch03.c.goal.axes: Rotating the axes changes the components; the vector and its magnitude $A$ stay the same
ch03.c.obs.drag: Drag the tip of $\vec A$ to change the vector
ch03.c.obs.neg: $\theta > 90^\circ$ gives $A_x < 0$: a component's sign refers to the axis direction
ch03.c.obs.rot: Rotate the axes: $A_x$ and $A_y$ change, $A$ does not
ch03.c.obs.incline: Axes at 30°: the coordinate choice for incline problems (Ch 5, 6)
ch03.s.obs.drag: Drag the tip of $\vec A$ or of $\vec B$
ch03.s.goal.para: Parallelogram rule: $\vec A + \vec B$ is the diagonal of the parallelogram with sides $\vec A$ and $\vec B$
ch03.s.obs.para: Dashed sides are $\vec A$ and $\vec B$ moved to the other tip, so the result matches head-to-tail addition
ch03.c.obs.comp: Drag the tip of $A_x$ or $A_y$ to change that component alone; $\vec A$, $A$ and $\theta$ follow
ch03.s.goal.comp: The components of the sum are the sums of the components: $C_x = A_x + B_x$, $C_y = A_y + B_y$
ch03.s.obs.panel: Top-left panel: $A_x + B_x = C_x$ and $A_y + B_y = C_y$ update as you drag
ch03.s.obs.cancel: When $\vec A$ and $\vec B$ point in opposite directions their components cancel, so $C < A + B$
